_comment: Sigma correlation rules (type: correlation) have no direct KQL/Lucene equivalent - a single query string cannot express 'count distinct X grouped by Y over time'. The elasticsearch/lucene Sigma backend explicitly refuses to convert them ('Backend does not support correlation rules'). The correct compile target is Kibana's native Threshold rule type, configured the same way the DCSync alert in this lab was built manually. This file documents that native rule config, generated from the Sigma correlation definition in rules/sigma/password_spraying_distributed_failures.yml.
name: Password Spraying - Multiple Failed Logons Across Distinct Accounts

params._note: Sigma's 'value_count field:TargetUserName gte:6' means 6+ DISTINCT usernames per source IP. Native Kibana Threshold rules count documents, not distinct field values, per group - so this config approximates the Sigma intent with document count as a proxy. For an exact distinct-count match, use a Cardinality aggregation via an Elasticsearch query rule (aggType: cardinality on winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) instead of the simpler Threshold rule shown here.
